newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Mandela confirms meeting jailed Timor rebel chief.
newsitem.headline: Mandela confirms meeting jailed Timor rebel chief.

text.p: South African President Nelson Mandela's office confirmed on Tuesday he had met jailed East Timorese rebel leader Xanana Gusmao during his state visit to Indonesia last week.

"The meeting was at President Mandela's request, in conformity with the South African government's commitment to promoting human rights and the peaceful resolution of conflicts," the president's office said in a statement.
But Mandela said he would not comment any further on the meeting, due to the sensitivity of negotiations taking place in the context of recent United Nations initiatives.

Gusmao, 50, serving a 20-year term for resisting Indonesia's annexation of East Timor, was brought from Jakarta's notorious Cipinang prison to the State Guest House adjacent to President Suharto's state palace for the meeting.

Suharto ordered thousands of Indonesian troops to invade East Timor in December 1975 after Portugal abandoned the colony the previous year and the left-leaning Fretilin party won a short and bitter civil war. Jakarta unilaterally annexed the territory the following year.
The United Nations has never recognised Indonesia's declaration of East Timor as its 27th province and still regards Portugal as the administering power.
U.N.-sponsored tripartite talks between Indonesia, Portugal and the U.N. Secretary-General on the future of East Timor have been going on for almost 15 years without result.
